title: Type 2 diabetes in adults: management
clean_text:
# GUIDELINE OBJECTIVES
This guideline covers the care and management of type 2 diabetes in adults (aged 18 and over). It focuses on patient education, dietary advice, managing cardiovascular risk, managing blood glucose levels, and identifying and managing long-term complications.

# RECOMMENDATIONS
Offer structured education to adults with type 2 diabetes and/or their family members or carers at and around the time of diagnosis, with annual reinforcement and review. Advise adults with type 2 diabetes that a low-fat, high-fibre diet, incorporating starchy carbohydrates and low glycaemic-index sources of carbohydrate is beneficial.

# TUBERCULOSIS TREATMENT GUIDANCE
Treatment of latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) is recommended for people at increased risk of progression to active tuberculosis disease. Preferred regimens include three months of once-weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine, four months of daily rifampin, or three months of daily isoniazid plus rifampin. Directly observed therapy is recommended for intermittent regimens.

# MONITORING
Clinicians should evaluate patients monthly for adherence, adverse effects and signs or symptoms of active tuberculosis disease throughout the course of LTBI treatment.

# MALARIA CHEMOPREVENTION
Seasonal malaria chemoprevention is recommended for children aged 3 to 59 months living in areas of highly seasonal malaria transmission across the Sahel sub-region of Africa. The intervention consists of the administration of monthly courses of amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine during the transmission season, up to four courses per season.

# IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS
Countries should adapt the number of cycles and timing of administration to the local pattern of malaria transmission, and integrate delivery with other child health interventions where feasible.
